heroBody: The AirPods Pro 3 launched with a new H3 chip, better active noise cancellation and heart-rate sensing, and Singapore pricing has been all over the place since: authorised Apple resellers hold the list price, while Amazon.sg, Shopee Mall and Lazada LazMall sellers undercut it by a meaningful margin during sale periods. This page pulls the live Singapore listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so you can see the current floor price, who is offering it, and whether the cheapest listing is a local set with Apple Singapore warranty or a parallel import.

highlightSectionTitle: What changed with the AirPods Pro 3

highlights.title: Noise cancellation and fit
highlights.body: The Pro 3 roughly doubles the effective noise cancellation of the Pro 2 thanks to the H3 chip and a redesigned ear tip with foam-infused silicone. If you commute on the MRT or work in open offices, this is the single biggest reason to pay the difference over a discounted Pro 2.

highlights.title: Heart-rate sensing and fitness
highlights.body: A tiny infrared sensor tracks heart rate during workouts and feeds Apple Fitness. It is a genuine differentiator for runners who do not want to wear a watch, but irrelevant if you only listen at a desk — in that case a Pro 2 on clearance is the smarter buy.

highlights.title: Battery and case
highlights.body: Listening time climbs to around eight hours with ANC on, and the case keeps the precision-finding U2 chip and lanyard loop. Charging is USB-C; the case no longer ships with a cable in some regions, so factor a cable into the price if you do not have one.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pay the least without getting burned
advicePoints: Check whether the listing says 'local set' or 'Apple Singapore warranty'. Parallel imports are cheaper but Apple Singapore stores will not service them under warranty.
Time it: Shopee and Lazada official stores discount deepest on 9.9, 10.10, 11.11, 12.12 and mid-month payday campaigns; Amazon.sg tends to match a few days later.
Stack vouchers before you compare: a higher sticker price with a platform coupon and cashback often beats the lowest raw listing.
Ignore listings well under the market floor with no reviews — they are usually pre-orders, refurbished units or bait-and-switch.
If you already own the Pro 2 and mostly use them at a desk, the upgrade is hard to justify; the money is better spent on the Pro 2 replacement tips or a case.
faqSectionTitle: AirPods Pro 3 in Singapore — common questions

faqs.question: Is the AirPods Pro 3 worth it over the AirPods Pro 2 in Singapore?
faqs.answer: If you rely on noise cancellation daily (MRT, flights, open office) or want heart-rate tracking without a watch, yes. If you mostly listen at home or at a desk, a discounted Pro 2 delivers most of the experience for noticeably less.

faqs.question: Do parallel-import AirPods Pro 3 come with Apple warranty in Singapore?
faqs.answer: No. Apple Singapore honours warranty for local sets only. Parallel-import listings carry the shop's own warranty, which is why they are cheaper.

faqs.question: When is the AirPods Pro 3 cheapest in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Historically during platform sale days (9.9, 11.11, 12.12) and payday campaigns on Shopee and Lazada, with Amazon.sg matching within days. Outside those windows the live prices on this page show the current floor.

faqs.question: Can I use AirPods Pro 3 with Android in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Yes for audio and basic noise cancellation, but adaptive audio, hearing features, seamless switching and find-my rely on an iPhone, so Android users get less value for the money.

categoryIntro.heading: Why Singapore AirPods prices vary so much
categoryIntro.body: Singapore has no single dominant electronics retailer, so the same Apple product is sold by the Apple Store, authorised resellers like Challenger and Courts, marketplace official stores and dozens of parallel importers at once. Prices move with platform campaigns rather than with Apple, which is why a static 'best price' article goes stale within days and why this page reads live listings instead.
